metadata.case_name: CHAU CHI WAH v. WONG KWOK MING

injuries.description: multiple contusions with superficial abrasions over the bilateral upper limbs and right lower limb.
injuries.body_part: bilateral upper limbs and right lower limb
source: Physical examination revealed multiple contusions with superficial abrasions over the bilateral upper limbs and right lower limb.
Dr. Poon noted that the Plaintiff had initially sustained multiple abrasions to both hands and the right lower limb, mild neck sprain, and soft tissue injury to the right shoulder.
injuries.icd_description: Strain or sprain of cervical spine, unspecified

injuries.description: rotator cuff tendinitis of the right shoulder
source: Examination revealed impingement and painful-arc signs and Dr. Pang diagnosed the Plaintiff’s injury to be rotator cuff tendinitis of the right shoulder.
Dr. Poon noted that the Plaintiff had initially sustained ... soft tissue injury to the right shoulder.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injury of muscle or tendon of the rotator cuff of shoulder

injuries.description: slight decrease in the right upper limb power and loss of muscle in the right forearm
source: The persistent symptoms in the right shoulder had led to slight decrease in the right upper limb power and loss of muscle in the right forearm.
injuries.icd_description: Injury of unspecified nerve at forearm level

injuries.description: about 30 degrees loss of end range right shoulder flexion
source: There was only minimal discomfort and feeling of a click at the subacromial space when the arm was raised to horizontal level, mild residual tenderness at the supraspinatus insertion on the great tuberosity, and about 30 degrees loss of end range right shoulder flexion.
injuries.icd_description: Strain or sprain of muscle or tendon of the rotator cuff of shoulder

manifestations.description: There was a certain degree of pain associated with the injury and the movement of the shoulder was restricted.
The multiple abrasions had recovered fully.
The neck symptoms had subsided and remained asymptomatic, apart from persistent mild pain and tenderness in the right trapezius muscle.
minimal discomfort and feeling of a click at the subacromial space when the arm is raised to horizontal level
mild residual tenderness at the supraspinatus insertion on the great tuberosity
about 30 degrees loss of end range right shoulder flexion
slight decrease in the right upper limb power and loss of muscle in the right forearm.
There were no sensory deficit and x-ray confirmed good alignment of the vertebrae with no fractures.

treatments_received: admitted to the Accident and Emergency Department of United Christian Hospital and discharged with oral analgesic
consultation with Dr. Pang Kin Wah, orthopaedic surgeon
assessment by Dr. Richard Poon, specialist in Orthopaedics and Traumatology
